title: List of video games that have better than player gen AI agents
author: Gkibarricade
selftext: Watched the Linesight YT channel's Trackmania AI. Post any GEN! AI's that have beat humans at video games.

comments.author: sirpalee
comments.body:
The AI used in Linesights trackmania videos is not considered GEN AI (generative ai), it's just reinforcement learning.

I think the elite dangerous team released some self-learning AI a few years ago (2016 or so), but they had to strip them of certain weapons, because the AI figured out how to beat players almost every time. Can't find the articles detailing it.

replies.author: Gkibarricade
replies.body: Not an expert but how is it not Generative if after every learning cycle there is a new generation. I thought that was considered under the umbrella not just AI that writes and draws.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body:
No. Generative AI are models that are capable of generating text, audio, images, video and other data based on user input.

You are thinking of the word "generation" which is often used to described how far along is an AI during training like reinforcement learning.

replies.author: Gkibarricade
replies.body: FPS AI sounds like the most impossible. It must be a bot with an AI on top. There is no way to teach 3d aiming.

replies.author: sirpalee
replies.body:
It's not impossible. There are several studies about it, I didn't read them but there is research toward it.

If the latest (ML based) tesla FSD can handle lots of traffic situationa, we can train a bot to playba simple fps game.

replies.author: MTOMalley
replies.body:
> There is no way to teach 3d aiming.

Pretty sure thats one of the first things you can set up with Unity's MLagents. 

If you can teach AI to balance a ball, you can teach it to aim up down left right :)

replies.author: Gkibarricade
replies.body: Not balance a ball but catch a particular ball while it's raining balls. Balance is easy because any movement will cause the ball to move and drop. But aiming has no consequences. We can use programming because we know what we are looking for (aka a shape on the screen and then aim at it). But without programming there is no reinforcement for aiming.

replies.author: MTOMalley
replies.body:
>But aiming has no consequences.


Thats why you code some consequences. Rewards and penalties is the process.

I think you should look at some content that follows Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO).As the person training the agent, you'll have to come up with rewards that make sense - but thats just part of the work. Aiming in 3d space has been done.

In reinforcement learning, you provide rewards based on the agent's actions, guiding it to improve over time. So while aiming might not have direct "consequences" like balancing a ball, you can set up rewards for successfully hitting targets, gradually teaching the AI to aim more accurately. It’s not about directly programming the AI to recognize shapes but rather letting it learn what actions lead to positive outcomes.
